pr_title: BUG: Don't cast categorical nan to int
pr_body:
- [x] closes #28406
- [x] passes `black pandas`
- [x] tests added / passed
- [x] whatsnew entry

This raises an error when attempting to cast a `Categorical` or `CategoricalIndex` containing `nans` to an integer dtype.  Also had to remove the casting within `get_indexer_non_unique` since this won't always be possible.
pr_comments: FWIW the issue with `test_get_indexer_non_unique ` is here https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/core/indexes/base.py#L4717.  If `target` is `Categorical` then the values can't always be cast to the dtype of the categories.
should the use_inf_as_na option matter here?

> should the use_inf_as_na option matter here?

Wasn't familiar with that option, but it shouldn't affect `numpy` behavior I think?

> I think this PR should focus on just NaN handling.
> 
> I'd rather see `Float64Index` properly handle astyping inf values to int (raise), and then do `self.categories.take(self.codes)` with a check if any of the codes is negative, so that we raise.

Ok, so for the purposes of this PR remove the references to `np.inf` in the code and tests?

That would be my preference. Did my earlier comment make sense?

The `NaN` issue can be solved by checking `Categorical.codes`

```python
In [7]: c = pd.Categorical([1, None, 2])

In [8]: c.codes < 0
Out[8]: array([False,  True, False])
```

The inf issue is deeper, and is present in Float64Index, so I think it should be split to its own PR.

```python
In [9]: c = pd.Categorical([1, np.inf])

In [10]: c.categories.astype(int)
Out[10]: Int64Index([1, -9223372036854775808], dtype='int64')
```

> That would be my preference. Did my earlier comment make sense?
> 
> The `NaN` issue can be solved by checking `Categorical.codes`
> 
> ```python
> In [7]: c = pd.Categorical([1, None, 2])
> 
> In [8]: c.codes < 0
> Out[8]: array([False,  True, False])
> ```
> 
> The inf issue is deeper, and is present in Float64Index, so I think it should be split to its own PR.
> 
> ```python
> In [9]: c = pd.Categorical([1, np.inf])
> 
> In [10]: c.categories.astype(int)
> Out[10]: Int64Index([1, -9223372036854775808], dtype='int64')
> ```

I believe so, you want to fix the `inf` casting behavior in one place (`Float64Index`) and then use the fixed `astype` method here?  Regarding the `nan` issue, is there a reason to prefer `self.codes < 0` over `self.isna()`?

issue_context.title: Converting from categorical to int ignores NaNs
issue_context.body:
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible
```python
In [6]: s = pd.Series([1, 0, None], dtype='category')                                                                                                                                                                                            

In [7]: s                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
Out[7]: 
0      1
1      0
2    NaN
dtype: category
Categories (2, int64): [0, 1]

In [8]: s.astype(int)                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
Out[8]: 
0                      1
1                      0
2   -9223372036854775808  # <- this is unexpected
dtype: int64
```
#### Problem description
When converting categorical series back into Int column, it converts `NaN` to incorect integer negative value.

#### Expected Output
I would expect that `NaN` in category converts to `NaN` in `IntX`(nullable integer) or `float`.

When trying to use `d.astype('Int8')`, I get an error `dtype not understood`

comments:
I would expect `s.atype(int)` to raise, the same as `s.astype(float).astype(int)`

To get a nullable integer, `s.astype("Int8")` should work, but let's leave that as a second issue (we may already have one for it, not sure).

> I would expect `s.atype(int)` to raise, the same as `s.astype(float).astype(int)`
> 
> To get a nullable integer, `s.astype("Int8")` should work, but let's leave that as a second issue (we may already have one for it, not sure).

It seems like the weird value gets introduced here: https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/core/arrays/categorical.py#L523 . Would this be a `numpy` issue?

```
In [1]: import numpy as np                                                      

In [2]: arr = np.array([1.0, 0.0, np.nan])                                      

In [3]: np.array(arr, dtype=np.int64)                                            
Out[3]: array([                   1,                    0, -9223372036854775808])
```

> I would expect s.atype(int) to raise, the same as s.astype(float).astype(int)

Well, but that's a bit sad because it means that once you convert to categoricals, you cannot get back :-( .

> It seems like the weird value gets introduced here: https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/core/arrays/categorical.py#L523 . Would this be a numpy issue?

Thanks for tracking it down. I think that's just NumPy's defined behavior.

We might want `astype_nansafe` there (should also test with `inf`).

>  Well, but that's a bit sad because it means that once you convert to categoricals, you cannot get back :-( .

What do you mean?

> What do you mean?

Well, I meant something like if you did `s = pd.Series([1, None]).astype(int).astype(category)` and now wanted to get back to `int` somehow. The workaround seems to be `s.astype('float').astype('Int8')` for example.

I understand it's tricky, especially when dealing with nullable integers. It's true that raising is probably better than trying to be somehow clever.

Sorry, I'm still not understanding. In your example,

```python
s = pd.Series([1, None]).astype(int)
```

raises. The conversion from float to int is what raises, not to or from categorical.

Sorry, I wrote it wrongly. I meant if you do:
```
In [3]: s = pd.Series([1, None], dtype='Int8').astype('category')
```
and now wanted to get back to numerics, or more specifically e.g. `Int8`. You have to do
```
In [6]: s.astype(float).astype('Int8')
```
while it would be super cool to do just `s.astype('Int8')`

> s.astype('Int8')

That should work just fine. As I said earlier

> To get a nullable integer, s.astype("Int8") should work, but let's leave that as a second issue (we may already have one for it, not sure).

> Thanks for tracking it down. I think that's just NumPy's defined behavior.
> 
> We might want `astype_nansafe` there (should also test with `inf`).

Seems that `astype_nansafe` expects an `ndarray` but `self` is Categorical here.  Any thoughts on the best workaround?

Hmm, OK.

It's a bit unfortunate, but I we'll need to include something like

```python
if is_integer_dtype(dtype):
    if self.isna().any():
        raise ValueError(...)
```

review_comments:
Kinda pedantic, but we can have other NA values here.

```python
In [18]: cat = pd.Categorical([pd.Timestamp('2000'), pd.NaT])
```

In this case, it's not a float that we're refusing to cast. So perhaps `Cannot convert NA to integer`.

Agree this seems more correct; do we want to think about consistency with `Series` as @jreback pointed out above?  Incidentally I just noticed that `Series` seems to be misbehaving as well in this special case, so probably worth a separate issue or PR:
